title: MWB mouse buttons not functioning in second screen VMWARE Workstation VM
author: thluther
summary: Mouse Without Borders can move the pointer on a remote PC, but VMware Workstation drops injected click, wheel, and keyboard events while its guest window has focus.
next_action: Approve a VMware-focused input-injection compatibility design and reproduce the focus transition.

confidence.rationale: The focus and event-class boundary is clear, but VMware's acceptance rules and whether PowerToys can safely work around them remain uncertain.

judgment.rationale: Multiple users reproduce Mouse Without Borders pointer movement reaching a VMware Workstation guest while clicks, wheel, and keyboard input are dropped whenever the VM owns focus. The focused-window boundary makes a targeted injection compatibility investigation possible.
evidence: The original report reproduces with Windows 11 hosts and VMware Player 17.5.0.
A later report on VMware Workstation 17.6.2 and PowerToys 0.100.2 confirms pointer motion works while clicks, scrolling, and keyboard input do not.
Unfocusing or minimizing VMware restores Mouse Without Borders input on the remote machine.
judgment.recommended_action: Approve a VMware-focused input-injection compatibility design and reproduce the focus transition.

fix_assessment.rationale: No existing fix attempt covers the scoped PowerToys-owned path identified by this lightweight judgment.

proposed_fixes.title: Use a VMware-compatible MWB input path for focused guests
proposed_fixes.root_cause: VMware's focused guest input capture accepts MWB pointer positioning but rejects or bypasses the injected button, wheel, and keyboard event path.
plan: Trace the exact event APIs, flags, integrity levels, and target window state used for pointer versus button/keyboard forwarding.
Test supported SendInput/raw-input-compatible alternatives and VMware enhanced-keyboard settings without weakening security boundaries.
If VMware intentionally rejects injected input, detect the focused guest and expose a clear compatibility limitation instead of silent partial control.
verification: Control a VMware Workstation 17.6.x guest through MWB and verify movement, clicks, wheel, and keyboard input.
Regression-test ordinary desktop apps, elevated windows, and non-VM fullscreen applications.

confidence.rationale: The focus and event-class boundary is clear, but VMware's acceptance rules and whether PowerToys can safely work around them remain uncertain.

issue_context.summary: Mouse Without Borders can move the pointer on a remote PC, but VMware Workstation drops injected click, wheel, and keyboard events while its guest window has focus.
known_information: Both source and destination hosts are Windows.
The failure is specific to a focused VMware guest window.
The issue persists through VMware Workstation 17.6.2 and PowerToys 0.100.2.
inferences: VMware's focused input-capture path distinguishes MWB's button/keyboard injection from pointer movement.
Integrity level, SendInput flags, raw-input capture, or VMware enhanced keyboard settings are plausible discriminators.
issue_context.analysis: The public report is sufficiently repeatable for maintainer-side testing. The design should first identify which injected event classes VMware rejects, then change MWB only if a compatible supported injection path exists.
initial_investigation: Reviewed all live confirmations, versions, focus behavior, labels, and timeline.
Found no linked fix, duplicate owner, or reporter evidence that normal local input fails.

actions.label: Approve VMware input-compatibility design
actions.design_summary: Identify and correct the MWB event path rejected by focused VMware guests
actions.note: Approval starts a separate fork-side design workflow; this lightweight judgment contains no full design and performs no GitHub write.
